title: Bobkov bound for normalized Boolean blocks
statement: Let $n,m$ be natural numbers with $m>0$. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $[0,1]$, and suppose it has a derivative $D(z)$ at every $z\in\mathbb R^n$, where $D(z)$ is a continuous linear functional on $\mathbb R^n$; assume the map $z\mapsto D(z)$ is globally $C$-Lipschitz for some $C\ge0$. For independent uniform bits $X_{ij}$, set $S(X)_i=m^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma(X_{ij})$, with $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$. Then $\overline I(\mathbb E f(S(X)))\le\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f(S(X)))^2+\sum_{i=1}^n D(S(X))(e_i)^2}+\sqrt{nm}\,2C/m$, where $e_i$ is the $i$th standard basis vector and the expectation is over the bits.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function on R^n with values in [0,1]
At every point, f has the specified Fréchet derivative D(z)
The derivative map D is globally C-Lipschitz
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,1]$ be differentiable with derivative family $D(z)$, globally $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm for the maximum norm, where $C\ge0$. Write $|D(z)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(D(z)e_i)^2}$. For independent uniform bits $X_{ij}$, put $S_r(X)_i=r^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^r(-1)^{X_{ij}}$. For every $m>0$, $\overline I(\mathbb E f(S_m(X)))\le\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f(S_m(X)))^2+|D(S_m(X))|_2^2}+\sqrt{nm}\,2C/m$.
